endorsements.quote: Fair models should not amplify existing inequities or underperform for marginalized populations.
Ultimately, maintaining human oversight and emphasizing interpretability are essential to ensure that causal digital twins enhance, rather than replace, clinical judgment [ 23 ].
Clinical decision-making should not be fully delegated to automated systems; rather, digital twins should serve as advisory tools that augment, but do not replace, physician judgment.
Clear accountability frameworks must be established to delineate the roles and responsibilities of model developers, clinical users, and institutional governance bodies.
Digital twins should be evaluated across demographic subgroups (e.g., age, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) to detect and mitigate disparate impacts.

unlisted_practices: Identify and mitigate biases in data collection such as missingness and selection bias when building digital twins.
Use privacy-preserving approaches such as de-identification, federated learning, and differential privacy to protect patient data used by digital twins.
Conduct sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of causal digital twins to unmeasured confounding.
Perform prospective validation of causal digital twin predictions where feasible.
Explicitly state causal assumptions (consistency, exchangeability, positivity, correct model specification) underlying digital twin counterfactual estimates.
Integrate interpretability tools such as SHAP or ICE plots into causal digital twins to make individualized treatment effects comprehensible to clinicians and patients.
Perform fairness and bias audits as an integral part of digital twin model validation.
Evaluate digital twins' counterfactual consistency by testing stability of predictions under small input perturbations.
Support interoperability standards such as HL7 FHIR or OMOP-CDM for digital twin integration into clinical workflows.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual and methodological framework paper proposing guidelines and a practical checklist for causal digital twins; it includes no empirical dataset or benchmark evaluations.
